title: Verbs with -ing or To
summary: Learn how to use two verbs together in English. You will discover when to use the -ing form and when to use to.

sections.p: Sometimes, when you use two verbs together, the second verb needs an -ing ending. We usually do this after verbs that talk about likes, dislikes, or finishing an action. For example, you enjoy doing something or you finish doing your work. Remember that the first verb changes for the past or present, but the second verb always keeps the -ing.

ex.en: I enjoy cooking dinner for my family.
ex.mean: I like the action of cooking.

ex.en: Do you mind waiting a few minutes?

sections.p: Other times, the second verb needs to come after the word 'to'. We often use this pattern after verbs that talk about plans, wants, or future hopes. For example, you want to buy something or you hope to travel soon. The word 'to' connects the two verbs together naturally.

ex.en: I want to learn Spanish this year.
ex.mean: It is my goal to study Spanish.

ex.en: We hope to visit Japan next summer.
He needs to buy a new phone.
ex.mean: It is necessary for him to get one.

sections.p: Good news! Some verbs can take either -ing or to with almost no change in meaning. Verbs like start, begin, and love are very friendly. You can say 'I love swimming' or 'I love to swim'. Both sentences are completely correct and mean the exact same thing.

tip: When you learn a new verb, always learn what comes after it. Make a list of verbs that take -ing and verbs that take to.

quiz.en: I enjoy ___ football with my friends on Saturdays.
She wants ___ a new car next month.
They hope ___ their grandparents during the holidays.
Please stop ___ so much noise while I am working.
We decided ___ at home because it was raining.
Do you mind ___ the window, please?
